title: Power-torsion kernel embeds in a deep ideal quotient
statement: For a map b:Q -> R of coherent modules on a Noetherian scheme X and an ideal K, if K^t ker(b)=0 for some positive t, then for some n the composite ker(b) -> Q -> Q/K^(n+1)Q is a monomorphism.

source.place: Tag 01YA (Artin-Rees), applied to the uniqueness argument of Tags 0889 and 088A

proof.text: The coherent-kernel closure theorem applied to b gives coherence of T = ker(b). The coherent/finite-type criterion gives quasi-coherence of T. Apply coherent_artin_rees to g = kernel.ι b.hom and Q to obtain c and its sectionwise intersection inclusion on every open.

Choose t >= 1 from hker and e = c+t. Write e = (c+t-1)+1. At e the Artin-Rees right-hand product is K^(e-c)T = K^t T. Its inclusion, and hence its composite with g, is zero because that product object is zero.

Let i:K^e Q -> Q be the product inclusion, f = g followed by the quotient projection, and k = kernel.ι f. The ideal product inclusion i is monomorphic because it is an image inclusion. The kernel condition gives (k followed by g) followed by cokernel.π i = 0. Mathlib Abelian.monoLift factors k followed by g through i. Therefore each section of k followed by g lies in both section ranges of i and g. Artin-Rees inclusion places it in the range of the zero map from step 2. Sectionwise extensionality proves k followed by g = 0.
Since g is a kernel inclusion, it is mono. Cancel g from k followed by g = 0 to get k = 0. Mathlib Abelian.mono_of_kernel_ι_eq_zero gives Mono f, yielding the required exponent n = c+t-1.

lean.statement:
theorem coherentMap_torsion_completion_ext_zero
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] (K : X.IdealSheafData)
    (Q R : CoherentModules X) (b : Q ⟶ R)
    (hker : ∃ t : ℕ, 1 ≤ t ∧
      IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower K.toModulesι t).2
        (kernel b.hom))) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, Mono (kernel.ι b.hom ≫ formalModuleQuotientπ K (n + 1) Q.obj)
